sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `openhands`
- Canonical name: OpenHands (`claim-openhands-sf-identity`; existing canonical `claim-openhands-identity` is not reused)
- Current status: actively shipped beta family. Agent Canvas is marked beta at 1.13.0 (`claim-openhands-sf-status`, `claim-openhands-sf-version-canvas`). Docs still pin an Agent Server image example at `1.26.0-python` (`claim-openhands-sf-version-agent-server`).
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15

Vendor strings are not collapsed: site copyright says OpenHands (`claim-openhands-sf-vendor-openhands`); community docs say All Hands AI, Inc. (`claim-openhands-sf-vendor-all-hands`); the Privacy Policy says All Hands AI (`claim-openhands-sf-vendor-privacy`).

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a software-engineering agent family with Agent Canvas, Software Agent SDK / Agent Server, hosted OpenHands Cloud, and OpenHands Enterprise (`claim-openhands-sf-what-it-is`, `claim-openhands-sf-architecture`).
- What it is not: Agent Canvas is not the agent runtime or sandbox (`claim-openhands-sf-what-it-is-not`). The FAQ says open-source OpenHands is not a multi-tenant product (`claim-openhands-sf-not-multi-tenant-oss`). The former Docker Local GUI is deprecated (`claim-openhands-sf-legacy-split`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `cloud-agent` inference matching `candidates.csv` (`claim-openhands-sf-primary-type`). The SDK engine sentence stays on the SDK page as architecture (`claim-openhands-sf-architecture-sdk-engine`). Keep both; do not average.
- Secondary roles: `control-plane` for Agent Canvas (`claim-openhands-sf-secondary-control-plane`); `cloud-agent` for OpenHands Cloud (`claim-openhands-sf-secondary-cloud-agent`).
- Agent-loop owner: the SDK Agent component owns the reasoning-action loop (`claim-openhands-sf-agent-loop-owner-sdk-agent`); Agent Server owns conversation start/resume/run/invoke/stream (`claim-openhands-sf-agent-loop-owner`); an ACP CLI owns a third-party agent's loop (`claim-openhands-sf-agent-loop-owner-acp`).
- Architecture: browser Canvas → selected backend; Agent Server, Automation Server, and workspace/sandbox stay separate (`claim-openhands-sf-architecture`). CLI source is `OpenHands/OpenHands-CLI`; former monorepo backend is archived at `OpenHands/legacy` (`claim-openhands-sf-legacy-split`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-local`, `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-remote`, `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-cloud`, `surface-openhands-desktop-macos`, `surface-openhands-desktop-windows`, `surface-openhands-cli-terminal`, `surface-openhands-cli-cloud`, `surface-openhands-cli-web`, `surface-openhands-cloud-web`, `surface-openhands-cloud-api`, `surface-openhands-cloud-slack`, `surface-openhands-cloud-jira`, `surface-openhands-tailscale`, `surface-openhands-ssh-web`, `surface-openhands-cli-acp`.
- Execution location: same-device host or Docker (`claim-openhands-sf-execution-local`); user-controlled remote Agent Server (`claim-openhands-sf-execution-remote`); that remote host, not the browser machine, is the execution boundary (`claim-openhands-sf-execution-remote-boundary`); vendor Cloud sandboxes (`claim-openhands-sf-execution-cloud`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: LiteLLM via the Agent SDK; first-party pages say a powerful model is required (`claim-openhands-sf-model-strategy`).
- Auth strategy: provider keys, OpenHands LLM key, ACP subscription reuse, or local/OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`claim-openhands-sf-auth-strategy`).
- Provider support: documented guides cover Bedrock, Azure, Google, Groq, local servers, LiteLLM Proxy, Moonshot, OpenAI, the OpenHands provider, and OpenRouter (`claim-openhands-sf-provider-support`). Local models include LM Studio, Ollama, Atomic Chat, vLLM, and SGLang (`claim-openhands-sf-local-models`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: `AGENTS.md` is always-on; skills use progressive disclosure; `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are recognized (`claim-openhands-sf-context-behavior`).
- Memory: opt-in two-tier `MEMORY.md` is off by default (`claim-openhands-sf-memory`). The When to Use page still says previous sessions are not remembered (`claim-openhands-sf-memory-faq-contradiction`).
- Compaction: SDK `LLMSummarizingCondenser` (`claim-openhands-sf-compaction`) plus Canvas manual Compact context (`claim-openhands-sf-compaction-canvas`).
- Session behavior: per-backend conversations with optional branch/archive/export (`claim-openhands-sf-session-behavior`). CLI stores settings and history under `~/.openhands` (`claim-openhands-sf-session-cli`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: SDK Bash, file editor, browser, and MCP (`claim-openhands-sf-tools`). Key Features UI tabs are chat, changes, embedded VS Code, terminal, app preview, and a non-interactive browser (`claim-openhands-sf-tools-ui`).
- Extensions: plugins that can include skills, hooks, MCP, agents, and commands; Claude Code plugin layout is accepted (`claim-openhands-sf-extensions`).
- MCP: documented as full support on CLI, SDK, Local GUI, and Cloud (`claim-openhands-sf-mcp`).
- Skills: Agent Skills spec plus triggers/paths; registry at OpenHands/extensions (`claim-openhands-sf-skills`).
- Hooks: `.openhands/hooks.json` on Cloud, CLI, and local GUI (`claim-openhands-sf-hooks`).
- APIs: Cloud V1 REST (`claim-openhands-sf-api`) and the Python SDK / Agent Server / OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`claim-openhands-sf-sdk-api`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: scheduled full conversations (`claim-openhands-sf-orchestration`); GitHub label/`@openhands` issue-to-PR (`claim-openhands-sf-orchestration-events`); built-in GitHub events and custom webhooks (`claim-openhands-sf-orchestration-event-automations`); Canvas `/goal` judge loop (`claim-openhands-sf-orchestration-goals`).
- Parallelism: TaskToolSet sub-agents are synchronous (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-subagents`). Canvas `launch_child_conversation` is a separate child-conversation path (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-child-conversations`). Parallel tool execution is experimental and defaults to sequential (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-tools`). Cloud/Enterprise scalable always-on agents (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-cloud`); Enterprise unlimited concurrent conversations (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-enterprise-unlimited`); Cloud API may pause older conversations (`claim-openhands-sf-parallelism-cloud-rate-limit`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: V1 providers are Docker, unsafe Process, and Remote (`claim-openhands-sf-isolation`). Canvas itself does not isolate (`claim-openhands-sf-isolation-canvas`). The Enterprise comparison table marks local isolated sandboxes as unavailable and VM isolation as on roadmap (`claim-openhands-sf-isolation-enterprise-table`).
- Permissions: SDK confirmation policies and security analyzers (`claim-openhands-sf-permissions`). Cloud API `waiting_for_confirmation` needs UI input (`claim-openhands-sf-permissions-cloud-api`).
- Security: safety depends on backend and mounts (`claim-openhands-sf-security`).
- Data path: local `~/.openhands` (`claim-openhands-sf-data-path-local`); Cloud Privacy Policy allows training and third-party AI providers (`claim-openhands-sf-data-path-cloud`); Enterprise claims data stays on customer infrastructure (`claim-openhands-sf-data-path-enterprise`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Keep native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell routes distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local web: `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-local` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-canvas-local`)
  - Remote client to user-controlled Agent Server: `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-remote` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-canvas-remote`)
  - Remote client to vendor Cloud: `surface-openhands-agent-canvas-cloud` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-canvas-cloud`)
  - Desktop preview: `surface-openhands-desktop-macos`, `surface-openhands-desktop-windows` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-desktop`)
  - CLI: `surface-openhands-cli-terminal` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-cli`)
  - CLI cloud start: `surface-openhands-cli-cloud` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-cli-cloud`)
  - CLI-in-browser: `surface-openhands-cli-web` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-cli-web`)
  - Cloud web: `surface-openhands-cloud-web` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-cloud-web`)
  - Cloud API: `surface-openhands-cloud-api` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-cloud-api`)
  - Slack: `surface-openhands-cloud-slack` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-slack`)
  - Jira Cloud dispatch: `surface-openhands-cloud-jira` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-jira`)
  - Tailscale: `surface-openhands-tailscale` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-tailscale`)
  - SSH to `openhands web`: `surface-openhands-ssh-web` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-ssh-web`)
  - IDE ACP: `surface-openhands-cli-acp` (`claim-openhands-sf-surface-acp-ide`)
- Remote behavior: Canvas → backend URL+key (`claim-openhands-sf-remote-access`). CLI cloud, Cloud web/API, Slack, Tailscale, and SSH stay on their own surface claims. Homepage Cloud URL `app.openhands.dev` and docs URL `app.all-hands.dev` are both recorded (`claim-openhands-sf-cloud-url-homepage`, `claim-openhands-sf-surface-cloud-web`).
- Mobile behavior: phone/tablet browser via Tailscale or authenticated ngrok (`claim-openhands-sf-mobile-access`); hosted Cloud from desktop and mobile is pricing copy (`claim-openhands-sf-mobile-access-cloud-pricing`). No native app established. Termux is not a primary target (`claim-openhands-sf-availability`).
- Background behavior: local npm/npx stops when the terminal closes; Docker/VM/Cloud continue (`claim-openhands-sf-background`). README says a cloud-hosted server continues when the laptop is shut (`claim-openhands-sf-background-readme-cloud`). Scheduled automations run a full conversation in a fresh sandbox (`claim-openhands-sf-background-scheduled`).

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Local OSS free; Individual Cloud free with BYOK or at-cost OpenHands models, 1 user and 10 daily conversations; Enterprise custom (`claim-openhands-sf-pricing`).
- License: MIT on Agent Canvas and software-agent-sdk (`claim-openhands-sf-license-mit`, `claim-openhands-sf-license-sdk`). Introduction says licenses are per repository (`claim-openhands-sf-license-split`). Enterprise vs OSS marks Cloud as Commercial SaaS and Enterprise as Commercial (`claim-openhands-sf-license-commercial`). Do not average OSS vs Cloud vs Enterprise.
- Maintenance: active beta (`claim-openhands-sf-maintenance`).
- Lock-in: unknown as a dedicated field. Related facts are commercial Cloud/Enterprise, Privacy Policy training/sharing, and ACP reuse of other vendors' CLIs (`claim-openhands-sf-data-path-cloud`, `claim-openhands-sf-license-commercial`, `claim-openhands-sf-compatibility-acp`).

sections.body:
- Lineage claims: renamed from OpenDevin (`claim-openhands-sf-lineage-opendevin`); GitHub org renamed from All-Hands-AI (`claim-openhands-sf-lineage-org-rename`).
- Relationship edges:

sections.body:
Use `comparison-neighborhoods.jsonl` memberships. None were written.

- Comparison neighborhood IDs: unknown
- Substitutes: unknown
- Partial substitutes: unknown
- Same-lineage relatives: unknown
- Often-confused products: unknown
- Complements: Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI are ACP targets, not neighborhood memberships (`claim-openhands-sf-compatibility-acp`).

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: inferred family map of Canvas + SDK/Agent Server + Cloud + Enterprise (`claim-openhands-sf-unique`). Classed `inference`, not official-docs.
- Meaningful drawbacks: unsandboxed local npm path (`claim-openhands-sf-drawback-local-isolation`); no multi-tenant OSS (`claim-openhands-sf-not-multi-tenant-oss`); session/context limits and weak frontend QA (`claim-openhands-sf-drawback-limits`); Individual Cloud 10 daily conversations (`claim-openhands-sf-drawback-individual-daily-cap`).
- Best fit: individuals and small teams on Agent Canvas; organizations that need RBAC/SAML/scale on Enterprise (`claim-openhands-sf-intended-user`).
- Not-for: vague or unreviewed sensitive work, exploratory visual design, and multi-tenant OSS sharing (`claim-openhands-sf-not-for`, `claim-openhands-sf-not-multi-tenant-oss`).
